sources.title: Lu Tian, STAT331: Unit 3 Kaplan-Meier (KM) Estimator
sources.locator: PDF pp. 1–12: risk-set event fractions and product-limit construction; Greenwood derivation on pp. 11–12; process Gaussian statement on p. 12.

contents.name: Risk-set event fractions and the Kaplan–Meier product limit
contents.reason: The definition records the failure count, risk count, tied-event convention, and product-limit formula with an explicit right-censoring endpoint convention.

contents.name: Greenwood first-order variance calculation
contents.reason: The local proof derives the stated plug-in Greenwood limit; the source's discrete-time delta calculation is a formula cross-check, not an exact finite-sample identity.

contents.name: Breslow–Crowley process Gaussian limit statement
contents.reason: The controlling design excludes process limits and confidence bands; this page proves only fixed-time terminal expansions under the stated counting-process contract.

sources.title: Lu Tian, STAT331 Unit 12: 1-Sample Problem: General Asymptotic Results
sources.locator: PDF pp. 5–10 and 12–14: Nelson–Aalen decomposition/consistency and variance clock, pointwise asymptotic route, exponential transform, Kaplan–Meier equivalence, and variance estimates.

contents.name: Nelson–Aalen compensator decomposition, positive-support condition, and consistency route
contents.reason: The page proves its random-risk-set denominator replacement locally by uniform empirical-risk convergence and finite-energy isometry; the source decomposition is used as a route cross-check.

contents.name: Pointwise Nelson–Aalen variance function
contents.reason: The source variance clock agrees with the locally proved integral of lambda over the positive at-risk probability and the terminal influence variance.

contents.name: Exponential transform and Kaplan–Meier asymptotic equivalence
contents.reason: The local proof bounds the continuous-time log-product remainder and applies the published finite-dimensional delta method at the fixed time.

contents.name: Process martingale CLT and confidence-band construction
contents.reason: The design forbids process bands, and the cited handout refers the functional martingale limit proof elsewhere; no such result is imported.

contents.name: Kaplan–Meier variance estimator comparison with Greenwood
contents.reason: The local compensator decomposition proves consistency of the requested Greenwood expression separately and does not identify it as an exact finite-sample variance.

sources.title: Qiqing Yu, Survival Analysis (Lecture Notes), Version 6/8/2010
sources.locator: PDF pp. 30–38, §§4.2.1–4.2.2: product-limit risk-set construction, last-censoring support boundary, finite-support consistency induction, and finite-support asymptotic delta calculation.

contents.name: Product-limit risk-set construction and residual tail mass after last censoring
contents.reason: The definition fixes the risk-set product convention, while the companion example proves nonidentifiability beyond a fixed censoring horizon by equal observed laws.

contents.name: Finite-support consistency induction from event-to-risk proportions
contents.reason: The local proof reproduces the finite ordered-support induction and states positivity at the target horizon explicitly.

contents.name: Finite-support asymptotic normality and delta calculation
contents.reason: The assigned design requires finite-support consistency and a separate continuous-time pointwise influence proof; no discrete-support asymptotic variance theorem is claimed here.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook, Chapter 8: Assessing Product Reliability
sources.locator: PDF pp. 103–104, §8.2.1.5: distribution-free Kaplan–Meier procedure, risk counts, and product-limit expression.

contents.name: Kaplan–Meier calculation steps and right-censored risk counts
contents.reason: The finite product and removal-from-risk-set convention agree with the locally stated estimator; the page also fixes the censoring-time convention.

contents.name: Worked reliability calculation with failures and withdrawals
contents.reason: The example performs its own hand arithmetic from the definition and uses the source only as an independent procedural cross-check.

contents.name: Modified plotting positions at the last failure
contents.reason: The assigned claim concerns the product-limit estimator and support loss; no plotting-position modification or complete-CDF tail extension is asserted.

sources.title: R. M. Dudley, Uniform Central Limit Theorems
sources.locator: Theorem 1.3 and proof, PDF pp. 1–2: probability transform and finite-grid proof of uniform empirical-distribution convergence.

contents.name: Uniform empirical-CDF convergence by finite grid
contents.reason: The local risk-set proof adapts the finite-grid argument to left limits so arbitrary censoring-time atoms are retained; the expected-square conclusion follows locally from boundedness.

sources.title: A. van der Vaart, Mathematical Statistics, ETH lecture notes
sources.locator: Theorem 6.4.1 and proof, PDF pp. 114–115: uniform empirical-distribution convergence from a finite partition and monotonicity.

contents.name: Glivenko–Cantelli finite-partition proof
contents.reason: This independent lecture-note proof cross-checks the finite-partition argument; the local proof separately handles one-sided CDF limits and the bounded expected-square conclusion.
